identity.title: Hierarchical Refinement: Optimal Transport to Infinity and Beyond

problem.claim: Scale optimal transport to large assignment problems while retaining a one-to-one correspondence.

gap.claim: Sinkhorn requires quadratic space, while low-rank OT uses linear space but cannot compute one-to-one correspondences.

contributions.claim: Shows that factors of an optimal low-rank coupling co-cluster each point with its Monge-map image in the assignment setting.
Introduces Hierarchical Refinement (HiRef), which recursively builds multiscale dataset partitions through low-rank OT subproblems and ends with a bijective coupling.
Reports linear space and log-linear runtime while addressing the limited resolution of low-rank OT.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish HiRef as a hierarchical low-rank-OT procedure that overcomes low-rank OT's correspondence-resolution limitation while preserving its space advantage.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report demonstrations on several datasets, including datasets with more than one million points.
The authors report scaling full-rank OT to problems previously beyond Sinkhorn's reach.
The authors report that HiRef uses linear space and log-linear runtime.

narrative_sequence.summary: OT aligns datasets through least-cost correspondences, with Sinkhorn's runtime efficiency contributing to its machine-learning success.
Sinkhorn's quadratic space limits larger datasets, whereas low-rank OT saves space but cannot produce one-to-one correspondences.
For assignment problems, the Monge map is guaranteed to be bijective; optimal low-rank coupling factors co-cluster points with their images.
HiRef uses this invariant for multiscale refinement, culminating in a bijective coupling with linear space and log-linear runtime.
The authors report experiments on several datasets, including ones exceeding one million points, and problems beyond Sinkhorn's prior reach.

source_observation.claim: The paper connects a structural invariant of low-rank couplings to a hierarchical algorithm that progressively restores correspondence resolution.

lessons.interpretation: A mathematically stated intermediate property can motivate both the algorithm's refinement mechanism and its claimed scalability-resolution tradeoff.
lessons.application: When proposing a scalable approximation, identify an invariant that preserves the target structure and use it to organize coarse-to-fine refinement.
lessons.exception: This move may not apply when the target correspondence is not an assignment problem or lacks the stated Monge-map structure.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset identities, baselines, quantitative accuracy, or runtime and memory measurements.
The scope and assumptions under which HiRef's bijective coupling and complexity claims hold beyond the stated assignment setting are not detailed.
